translations.literal: The cup-raisers give mare's milk to those who hit to drink—Court of Imperial Entertainments officials hold this office.
translations.idiomatic: The cup-raisers give mare's milk to those who hit the mark to drink—Court of Imperial Entertainments officials hold this office.

sentences.zh: 請射者，掌定耦射。

translations.literal: The shooting-requesters manage forming pairs for shooting.
translations.idiomatic: The shooting-requesters manage forming pairs for shooting.

sentences.zh: 射畢，再請某耦射，侍儀司職之。

translations.literal: When shooting is finished, they again request such-and-such a pair to shoot—the Ceremonial Attendants Directorate holds this office.
translations.idiomatic: When shooting is finished, they again request such-and-such a pair to shoot—the Ceremonial Attendants Directorate holds this office.

sentences.zh: 待獲者、掌矢納於司射器者，以隸僕供其役。

translations.literal: Retrievers and those who place arrows in the archery master's vessel are supplied by menial servants.
translations.idiomatic: Retrievers and those who place arrows in the archery master's vessel are supplied by menial servants.

sentences.zh: 執旗者六人，掌於容後執五色旗。

translations.literal: Six banner-bearers hold the five-colored banners behind the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Six banner-bearers hold the five-colored banners behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 如射者中的，舉紅旗應之。

translations.literal: If the shooter hits the center, they raise the red banner in response.
translations.idiomatic: If the shooter hits the center, they raise the red banner in response.

sentences.zh: 中採，舉採旗應之。

translations.literal: If he hits a colored fold, they raise the colored banner in response.
translations.idiomatic: If he hits a colored fold, they raise the colored banner in response.

sentences.zh: 偏西，舉白旗。

translations.literal: If the shot misses toward the west, they raise the white banner.
translations.idiomatic: If the shot lands off-center toward the west, they raise the white banner.

sentences.zh: 偏東，舉青旗。

translations.literal: If the shot misses toward the east, they raise the green banner.
translations.idiomatic: If the shot lands off-center toward the east, they raise the green banner.

sentences.zh: 過於鵠舉黃旗。

translations.literal: If the shot passes beyond the target, they raise the yellow banner.
translations.idiomatic: If the shot passes beyond the target, they raise the yellow banner.

sentences.zh: 不及鵠，舉黑旗。

translations.literal: If it falls short of the target, they raise the black banner.
translations.idiomatic: If it falls short of the target, they raise the black banner.

sentences.zh: 軍士二人掌之。

translations.literal: Two soldiers manage this.
translations.idiomatic: Two soldiers manage this.

sentences.zh: 引禮二，掌引文武官進退，侍儀司舍人職之。

translations.literal: Two ushers manage leading civil and military officials forward and back—Ceremonial Attendants Directorate clerks hold this office.
translations.idiomatic: Two ushers lead civil and military officials forward and back—Ceremonial Attendants Directorate clerks hold this office.

sentences.zh: 太祖又以先王射禮久廢，弧矢之事專習於武夫，而文士多未解，乃詔國學及郡縣生員皆令習射，頒儀式於天下。

translations.literal: The founding emperor further held that the archery rites of former kings had long been abandoned, bow and arrow skills were practiced only by military men while most literati did not understand them; he therefore ordered students of the National University and prefectural and county schools all to practice archery and promulgated the protocol throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor further held that the archery rites of former kings had long been abandoned, bow and arrow skills were practiced only by military men while most literati did not understand them; he therefore ordered students of the National University and prefectural and county schools all to practice archery and promulgated the protocol throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 朔望則於公廨或閒地習之。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month they practiced at government offices or open ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month they practiced at government offices or open ground.

sentences.zh: 其官府學校射儀，略仿大射之式而殺其禮。

translations.literal: The archery protocol for government offices and schools followed the grand archery form in outline but reduced the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The archery protocol for government offices and schools followed the grand archery form in outline but reduced the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 射位初三十步，自後累加至九十步。

translations.literal: The shooting position began at thirty paces and was progressively increased to ninety paces.
translations.idiomatic: The shooting position began at thirty paces and was progressively increased to ninety paces.

sentences.zh: 射四矢，以二人爲耦。

translations.literal: Four arrows were shot, with two persons forming a pair.
translations.idiomatic: Four arrows were shot, with two persons forming a pair.

sentences.zh: 永樂時有擊球射柳之制。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign there were regulations for polo and willow-shooting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign there were regulations for polo and willow-shooting.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月五日幸東苑，擊球射柳，聽文武羣臣四夷朝使及在京耆老聚觀。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month of the eleventh year he visited the Eastern Park for polo and willow-shooting, permitting civil and military officials, envoys from the four directions, and elders in the capital to gather and watch.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month of the eleventh year he visited the Eastern Park for polo and willow-shooting, permitting civil and military officials, envoys from the four directions, and elders in the capital to gather and watch.

sentences.zh: 分擊球官爲兩朋，自皇太孫而下諸王大臣以次擊射，賜中者幣布有差。

translations.literal: Polo players were divided into two teams; from the imperial great-grandson down, princes and great ministers shot in order; those who hit were granted silks and cloth in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Polo players were divided into two teams; from the imperial great-grandson down, princes and great ministers shot in order; those who hit were granted silks and cloth in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: ○救日伐鼓

translations.literal: Rescuing the sun and beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: Rescuing the sun and beating drums during eclipse.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年二月，定救日食禮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Hongwu, the rite for rescuing a solar eclipse was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Hongwu, the rite for rescuing a solar eclipse was fixed.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝常服，不御正殿。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor wore ordinary dress and did not preside in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor wore ordinary dress and did not preside in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 中書省設香案，百官朝服行禮。

translations.literal: The Secretariat set out an incense table; officials in court dress performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat set out an incense table; officials in court dress performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 鼓人伐鼓，復圓乃止。

translations.literal: Drummers beat the drums; when the sun returned to fullness they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Drummers beat the drums; when the sun returned to fullness they stopped.

sentences.zh: 月食，大都督府設香案，百官常服行禮，不伐鼓，雨雪雲翳則免。

translations.literal: For a lunar eclipse, the Commander-in-Chief's Office set out an incense table; officials in ordinary dress performed the rite without beating drums; if there was rain, snow, or cloud cover the rite was waived.
translations.idiomatic: For a lunar eclipse, the Commander-in-Chief's Office set out an incense table; officials in ordinary dress performed the rite without beating drums; if there was rain, snow, or cloud cover the rite was waived.

sentences.zh: 二十六年三月更定，禮部設香案於露臺，向日，設金鼓於儀門內，設樂於露臺下，各官拜位於露臺上。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-sixth year it was revised: the Ministry of Rites set an incense table on the open terrace facing the sun; set gold drums inside the ceremonial gate; set music below the terrace; each official's bowing position was on the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-sixth year it was revised: the Ministry of Rites set an incense table on the open terrace facing the sun; set gold drums inside the ceremonial gate; set music below the terrace; each official's bowing position was on the terrace.

sentences.zh: 至期，百官朝服入班，樂作，四拜興，樂止，跪。

translations.literal: When the time came, officials in court dress entered ranks; music played; they performed four bows and rose; music stopped; they knelt.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, officials in court dress entered ranks; music played; they performed four bows and rose; music stopped; they knelt.

sentences.zh: 執事者捧鼓，班首擊鼓三聲，衆鼓齊鳴，候復圓，復行四拜禮。

translations.literal: Attendants bore the drums; the lead official struck three beats; all drums sounded together; they waited until the sun returned to fullness, then performed four bows again.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants bore the drums; the lead official struck three beats; all drums sounded together; they waited until the sun returned to fullness, then performed four bows again.

sentences.zh: 月食，則百官便服於都督府救護如儀。

translations.literal: For a lunar eclipse, officials in informal dress performed the rescue rite at the Regional Military Commission according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: For a lunar eclipse, officials in informal dress performed the rescue rite at the Regional Military Commission according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 在外諸司，日食則於布政使司、府州縣，月食則於都指揮使司、衛所，如儀。

translations.literal: In outer offices, for solar eclipse at the provincial administration commission, prefecture, and county; for lunar eclipse at the regional military commission and guard post—according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In outer offices, solar eclipses were handled at the provincial administration commission, prefecture, and county; lunar eclipses at the regional military commission and guard post—according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，大喪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing there was a great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Longqing there was a great mourning.

sentences.zh: 方成服，遇日食。

translations.literal: Just as mourning dress had been assumed, a solar eclipse occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Just as mourning dress had been assumed, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 百官先哭臨，後赴禮部，青素衣、黑角帶，向日四拜，不用鼓樂。

translations.literal: Officials first went to wail at the mourning hall, then proceeded to the Ministry of Rites in blue plain dress and black horn belt, performed four bows facing the sun, without drums or music.
translations.idiomatic: Officials first went to wail at the mourning hall, then proceeded to the Ministry of Rites in blue plain dress and black horn belt, performed four bows facing the sun, without drums or music.
